title: Abu Talib dies
hookLine: the uncle who protected him dies in the same year, and the shield is gone

cards: Dust, thrown from the street onto his head as he walks home through Mecca. He goes home with it still in his hair, and his daughter, crying, gets up to wash it off.

He says to her: don't cry, my daughter, Allah will protect your father. Ibn Ishaq tells why it could happen now, when it couldn't before: the man who had kept the street from touching him was gone. Today: Abu Talib.

teach.h: THE UNCLE WHO WOULDN'T HAND HIM OVER.
teach.b: Abu Talib was his uncle, the one who took him in as a boy and, as the sirah tells it, refused again and again to hand him over when the leaders of Quraysh came asking.
He led the clan into the valley during the boycott rather than give him up. He was the shield. Then, in the same year as Khadijah, Ibn Ishaq says, he is dying.
Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the scene at his bedside. The Prophet comes in and finds two leaders of Quraysh already there, Abu Jahl among them.
He says to his uncle: say there is no god but Allah, a word I can plead for you with before Allah. The two men answer: will you leave the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?

In Bukhari's report his last words hold to the religion of Abd al-Muttalib, his father. The Prophet says he will keep asking forgiveness for him unless he's forbidden. Muslims read this scene in different ways.

In the Sunni hadith collections it stands as the account of his death, and the report itself links it to two verses, one of them in surah twenty-eight, saying that the Prophet does not guide whom he loves; Allah guides whom He wills.
Shia Muslims hold that Abu Talib was a believer who kept his faith quiet to keep his protection strong, and they honor him as such.

teach.h: A SHIELD IS SEEN WHEN IT'S GONE.
teach.b: Both remember the same thing about his life: he protected his nephew when it cost him.
Then the protection was gone, and the dust in the street is how the sirah shows it. Often nobody sees a shield until it isn't there.
This week was full of shields: a just king, Meccans of conscience, a wife who held him up. Now the shield of his own clan falls.

how: Muslims learn Abu Talib's protection and death as part of the Meccan sirah; Sunni and Shia Muslims understand his faith differently, and Shia Muslims honor him as a believer.

games.why: Bukhari reports he asked for that word, so he could plead for his uncle with it before Allah.

practice: Think back over your life for the people who stood between you and something hard: a parent, an older sibling, a teacher who covered for you, a friend who said, leave them alone.
Pick one who is still living, and see what they did and what it cost them. If you pray, you can ask Allah to reward them, as Muslims often do.

wordCard.voice: Abu Talib. The uncle who protected him through the boycott dies, and the street can reach him. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name the uncle was known by, 'father of Talib'.

carryVoice: Your line: the shield is gone. Remembered, in every reading, for his care. See you tomorrow.
